write_path.workload: One bulk SQL INSERT of synthetic recovery_ingress_receipts; each row executes the normal per-tenant append-only audit trigger. Every trial ran inside an explicit transaction and was rolled back.

exploratory_first_post_index.note: Cold/noisy managed-host run; excluded from steady-state baseline.

ten_thousand_findings_with_eleven_thousa.critical_note: 163.681 ms is acceptable for a human-facing query at this synthetic size, but is materially slower than other tested reads and is not evidence of good 100K/1M scaling.

application_hardening: Dashboard KPIs now aggregate over the full tenant population instead of incorrectly using the limited top-100 review queue.
Dashboard review queue resolves the latest review state in SQL instead of loading every tenant disposition into application memory.
Confirmed-findings endpoint resolves latest review state in SQL and caps the response at 500 rows.
Payments endpoint limits authorization/event reads to the 250 payment instructions actually returned.
Payment analytics and confirmed-count analytics compute latest state in PostgreSQL instead of materializing entire histories in JavaScript.
indexes: recovery_audit_chain_head_idx ON recovery_audit_events(tenant_id, occurred_at DESC, id DESC)
recovery_findings_review_queue_idx ON recovery_challenge_findings(tenant_id, variance_cents DESC, id)
recovery_review_latest_idx ON recovery_review_dispositions(tenant_id, finding_id, created_at DESC, id DESC)
recovery_payment_event_latest_idx ON recovery_payment_events(tenant_id, instruction_id, occurred_at DESC, created_at DESC, id DESC)
recovery_payment_instruction_recent_idx ON recovery_payment_instructions(tenant_id, created_at DESC, id DESC)
claim_boundary: Database write results are bulk-statement throughput, not HTTP/API requests per second.
All performance fixtures were synthetic and rolled back; no customer data was used.
Tests were single-tenant and did not prove concurrent multi-tenant throughput or lock contention behavior.
No 100K or 1M persisted database population benchmark has been executed.
The confirmed-list query is the clearest measured database performance concern and needs higher-scale testing before any enterprise-latency claim.
Managed database warmup/cache/scheduling materially affected exploratory timings.
